newsitem.title: USA: Missouri corn, soybean plantings top average pace.
newsitem.headline: Missouri corn, soybean plantings top average pace.

text.p: Missouri's corn and soybean plantings were running ahead of the five-year average in the week ended Sunday, according to the weekly Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service report.

Corn was 71 percent planted, 11 days behind a year ago but two weeks ahead of the five-year average. Soybeans were nine percent seeded, ahead of both last year and the five-year average of six percent.
Sorghum was 17 percent planted, also ahead of 11 percent last year and 16 percent for the five-year average.
Cotton was 46 percent planted, against 32 percent average.
Winter wheat conditions improved slightly during the week with one percent rated very poor, seven percent poor, 27 percent fair, 55 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
About 30 percent of the wheat crop was heading, ahead of the five-year average of 25 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, 11 percent short, 69 percent adequate and 19 percent surplus.
Pasture and range conditions were rated one percent very poor, 10 percent poor, 37 percent fair, 47 percent good and five percent excellent, nearly unchanged from a week ago.
